summary.headline: Gateway Distriparks Q4 FY26: West Asia disruption keeps volumes subdued; Q4 rail-plus-CFS volume about 188,000 TEUs, with management guiding Snowman's INR1,000 crore revenue target to slip about a year.
summary.overview: Management said West Asia-linked disruption continued into April, with import cargo from the US, Europe and Middle East and export food cargo (rice, frozen foods) affected, and no clarity on recovery. Q4 volumes were about 188,000 TEUs (96,000 rail, 91,000 CFS), and double-stacking averaged 40% for FY26 (42% in Q4). Snowman's margins fell in FY26 on warehouse start-up costs, DG power costs and a 5PL one-time procurement, while employee costs rose on headcount build-up for Ankleshwar and retention bonuses. Management is still pursuing expansion (Indore targeted for FY28, Jaipur pending a July court hearing) and a long-term 15% rail and Snowman growth target, while gross debt has fallen to about INR170 crore standalone.

segments.name: Rail (container train operations)
segments.commentary: Rail volume about 96,000 TEUs in Q4. Management targets about 15% long-term rail growth as new terminals are added; FY26 rail throughput about 494,000 vs about 333,000 in FY22 (about 4.3% CAGR, per analyst).

segments.name: CFS (container freight station)
segments.commentary: CFS volume about 91,000 TEUs in Q4; management targets about 5% growth. Company has stated it is not actively seeking a buyer for the CFS business.

segments.name: Snowman Logistics (cold chain)
segments.commentary: Warehousing and 5PL margins fell in FY26 on start-up warehouses in Kolkata and Krishnapatnam, power and DG costs; 5PL gross margin said to be roughly flat YoY. Target of INR1,000 crore revenue at about 15% blended EBITDA margin (about INR150 crore EBITDA) now likely deferred about a year to FY29.

guidance_outlook: Snowman revenue target INR1,000 crore still the plan; management says it may slip about a year, with FY29 seen as more realistic than FY28.
Long-term growth targets: about 15% for rail and Snowman, about 5% for CFS, subject to new terminal additions and disruptions.

Capex: Indore ICD about INR150 crore total (about INR50 crore spent on land, about INR100 crore over next 2 years); Jaipur about INR70 crore if approved; about INR125 crore for electric reach stackers, EVs, three rakes and a new warehouse; Snowman FY27 capex guideline about INR50 crore.
Tax: MAT rate cut by 1%, but ATI tax benefit lost; management expects no cash tax for 3-4 years using MAT credit.
Indore ICD target commencement of operations in 2028; Ankleshwar ICD expected to take 3-6 months more for permissions.
Management expects West Asia recovery timing to determine FY27 volumes and whether one-time domestic start-up and empty haulage costs recur.
capex_capacity: Indore ICD: INR150 crore project, about INR50 crore spent on land; Ankleshwar MMLP (Sawariya Group) domestic volumes ramping month-on-month, with steel coil rake handling for ArcelorMittal added this quarter.
Jaipur ICD: stuck; next hearing in July for final arguments; management hopeful of a positive order then or shortly after.
Land bank said to support up to 4x current ICD volume; yard extensions planned at Garhi and Piyala when utilisation reaches 70-80%.
Fleet: about 250-260 owned trailers plus about 200 leased; EV trailers at about INR90 lakh blended cost; three rakes being bought; solar and EV charging infrastructure planned.
Management is not looking to increase its Snowman stake in the near term.
demand_pricing: West Asia disruption continuing: import cargo from US, Europe and Middle East affected; export food, rice and frozen cargo hit; April trend similar to March, not materially worse.
Snowman: dry share of capacity being cut from about 9-10%, shifting frozen cargo in to lift yields; price increases passed through on contract renewals, including wage-law related costs in Haryana.

LCL and time-sensitive cargo opportunity in NCR estimated at 6,000-10,000 TEUs per month, but no conversion yet because shippers are protecting current volumes; JNPT DFC double-stack operation still pending by a couple of months.
Management declined to share regional market share figures; said market share is broadly intact versus recent quarters.
Competition: Snowman claims market leadership; second organised competitor about half its pallet capacity and reducing further.

qa_highlights.question: Current volume trend given West Asia disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Samvid Gupta said volumes remain subdued with no clarity on recovery; a wait-and-watch situation. Rajguru Behgal said import cargo from US, Europe and Middle East and food, rice and frozen exports were affected.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise about 12-13% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Samvid Gupta said it reflects headcount additions for domestic scaling (ahead of Ankleshwar) plus retention bonuses.

qa_highlights.question: Snowman margin decline and capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Padamdeep Handa cited R&M, start-up power costs at new warehouses and high DG costs; utilisation averaged about 86-87% in FY26 including newly onboarded facilities.

qa_highlights.question: Snowman debt and lease obligations for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Raghav Garg said about INR30 crore of debt repayments are due in FY27, with lease rent of about INR40 crore a year charged to operating expense.

qa_highlights.question: Why did realisation and margin per TEU fall YoY and QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Samvid Gupta cited import-export imbalance, more empty and underframe moves, lower laden 40-foot volume, train stabling costs in March, and upfront domestic costs (empty haulage and container leases without matching revenue).

qa_highlights.question: Can 15% rail growth be achieved given FY22-FY26 throughput CAGR of about 4.3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Samvid Gupta said rail grew about 10% last year, above market growth, through share gains and domestic volumes; growth to come from Ankleshwar, Indore and Jaipur, with new locations also planned.

risks_watch: Duration of West Asia and US-Iran disruption; April trend similar to March with no clear end date.

Snowman INR1,000 crore revenue target and 15% EBITDA margin target deferred, possibly to FY29; limited disclosure of cash flow below EBITDA (lease rentals) despite investor requests, with a reporting system promised from next quarter.
Jaipur ICD legal outcome at July hearing; Indore ICD commissioning in 2028.
Cost pressures: fixed costs on lower volume, stabling and empty haulage costs, DG power costs; employee cost growth ahead of volumes.
Transport segment under stress; new transport management system going live in about a month; management keeps the owned fleet rather than outsourcing.
Cash position: about INR14 crore cash on hand at March end against about INR30 crore FY27 debt repayments.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term asset plans and debt reduction, but cautious and non-committal on near-term volumes, Snowman targets and cash flow disclosure. Management repeatedly tied outcomes to the West Asia situation and declined to give concrete figures on competition and market share.
key_quotes: So, volumes remain a bit subdued, and there's no clarity also on when things will pick up exactly. So, it's a wait-and-watch kind of situation.
It's a 15% EBITDA margin on a blended basis, and we have a INR150 crores EBITDA.
But maybe more realistic is FY '29.
So, we're not stopping our search for land in the right locations for more ICDs.
